item.text: The server applies Chi’s `RealIP` middleware, which can rewrite `RemoteAddr` from forwarding headers. I’ll preserve the transport peer address before that middleware and use it for the whitelist check, so a client supplied forwarding header cannot grant proxy authentication.

The backend now builds a proxy session only after the transport peer matches the configured whitelist. It creates a user on first trusted login, updates the login time, and sends the session in the UI config. I’ve also wired that session into the frontend’s existing local storage fields and added recursive map redaction. Next I’m checking the relevant tests and edge cases.

item.text:
Implemented trusted reverse proxy login. `ReverseProxyWhitelist` accepts comma-separated IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs, ignores invalid entries, and supports `@` for Unix sockets. Trusted requests use `ReverseProxyUserHeader` (default `Remote-User`), with optional `ReverseProxyDefaultUser`. Successful login creates a user when needed, issues a token, updates the login time, and initializes the frontend session. Untrusted requests receive no `auth` payload. I also added nested log redaction and marked the index response `no-store`.

Verification passed: Go tests for `server/app`, `log`, and `server`; 35 UI tests; formatting and diff checks.
